fields.meta_description: Build a post purchase survey that asks where buyers found you, checks each delivery, and times reorder reminders. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Post Purchase Survey for the Moment After Checkout
fields.hero_description: Get a post purchase survey that ties each answer to its order, from first-order source to fit and delivery problems.
fields.features_heading: What Buyers See and Where Their Answers Go
fields.features_subheading: The first three shape the survey a buyer opens after checkout. The last three decide what happens to each answer once it is in.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written for your store

Describe the store, the product, and the decision each answer should inform. Emergent writes the survey from that prompt, and one more sentence rewords or adds a question.
fields.feature_2:
Follow-ups that branch on the first answer

A buyer who says the pants run small gets one more question about the size they ordered. A buyer who found you through a friend skips it. You describe each branch in plain English.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Buyers who open the link from a shipping text see one question on each screen. A two-question survey takes two taps, with no long form to scroll through on a small screen.
fields.feature_4:
Each answer saved with its order number

The app connects to your store platform through its API and attaches the order number, the products, and the ship date to each response. Answers can sync to your CRM as well.
fields.feature_5:
Problem answers sent to the right person

As soon as a buyer reports a damaged box or a missing item, the app posts it to a Slack channel, sends an email, or raises an in-app alert, with the order number attached.
fields.feature_6:
Responses kept in a database you own

Every answer lands in a database your team owns, with no cap on the number of responses you collect. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository as well.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Stores and What Buyers Told Them
fields.tab_content_1:
Podcast listeners placed 137 first orders in October

Wickfern Candle Co. asks first-time buyers one question on the order confirmation page: how did you first hear of the shop? In October, 412 answer. A podcast ad leads with 137, ahead of a friend at 104, Instagram at 98, and search at 73. The shop books another quarter of podcast spots.
fields.tab_content_2:
Damaged and missing items reach support the same day

When the carrier marks a Pantrywell box delivered, the buyer gets a text asking whether it arrived complete and intact. Of 268 answers in one week, 241 say yes, 15 say late, 9 say damaged, and 3 report a missing item. Each damaged or missing answer posts to the support channel in Slack with its order number.
fields.tab_content_3:
64 of 150 Talus buyers say it runs small

Fernpath Outfitters waits 10 days after delivery, then asks buyers of the Talus hiking pant how it fits against their usual size. Of 150 answers, 64 say it runs small, 71 say true to size, and 15 say it runs large. The team adds a note to the product page suggesting one size up.
fields.tab_content_4:
Reorder reminders timed to each buyer's own answer

Brewlark Coffee asks one-time buyers how long a bag will last them. Of 196 answers, 58 pick 2 weeks, 81 pick 3 weeks, and 39 pick 4 weeks, and the app emails each of those 178 buyers a reorder reminder in the week they chose. The other 18 say they will not buy again and get one question about why.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Post Purchase Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a post purchase survey, build it with Emergent, and send each answer where it can act.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the decision each question feeds
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one decision per question: which channel gets more ad budget, which warehouse needs better packing, which size chart needs a note. Cut any question that changes nothing. Two or three questions are enough for a first version.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about the order source on the confirmation page, while the purchase is fresh. Ask about the delivery once the box is marked delivered, and save fit or reorder questions until the buyer has used the product for a week or two.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent which store the survey is for, then list the questions, the answer options, and any follow-up a given answer should trigger. Emergent builds the survey and a dashboard for its answers from that prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the store through its API so each response arrives with its order. Check one recent order first and confirm the order number and products sit beside the answer before you rely on the data.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Name an owner for problem answers
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which answers need a person, such as a broken jar or a short shipment, and name who handles them. Route each one to that person in Slack or by email.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Place a real order and answer it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Place a real order, or reuse a recent one, and answer the survey on a phone. Confirm the answer saved under the right order and that a problem answer reached its owner.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and read the first week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the survey and put its link on the confirmation page, in the shipping email, or in the delivery text. After a week, read the counts and reword any question whose answers are not informing a decision.

faq_plan.q: What is a post purchase survey?
faq_plan.a: A post purchase survey is a short set of questions a buyer answers after placing an order, on the confirmation page or later by email or text. It asks what only the buyer knows at that point: where they heard of the store, whether the box arrived intact, how the product fits, and whether they plan to order again.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a post purchase survey?
faq_plan.a: Write one prompt for Emergent's AI survey builder that names the store, what you want to learn from buyers, and what should happen when an answer signals a problem. Emergent builds the survey with its database and dashboard, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Test it on one real order before the link goes live.

faq_plan.q: How many post purchase survey questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with one to three on the confirmation page, and keep any follow-up email to five or fewer. Each question should feed a decision you will make. Cut any that would not. Once the first answers show what is missing, you can add a question by prompting Emergent again.

faq_plan.q: What are some post purchase survey examples for an online store?
faq_plan.a: Three examples that go beyond order source and delivery: What almost stopped you from ordering today? Is this order a gift? Did you look at another store before buying? The gift and comparison questions work as a yes no questions survey, with one open follow-up for anyone who answers yes.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in post-purchase survey software?
faq_plan.a: Look for four things: the survey can appear on your confirmation page and in emails, each answer is saved with its order number, a problem answer can alert a person, and you can export the data. With Emergent, the survey is an app you build, and its responses sit in a database you own with no response cap.

faq_plan.q: How soon after delivery should a post-purchase survey go out?
faq_plan.hint: How to use a post purchase survey?
faq_plan.a: Send the delivery question within 24 hours of the box being marked delivered, while the unboxing is fresh. Questions about fit or how fast a product runs out can wait until the buyer has used it. Send one reminder about three days later to anyone who has not answered, then stop.

faq_plan.q: Is it okay to add humor to a post-purchase survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if it suits the brand and stays out of the way of the answer. Borrow a line from a list of funny survey questions for the thank-you screen or one answer option, but keep the question itself plain so the answers stay easy to count. A candle shop can sound warmer than a pharmacy.

faq_plan.q: How do I tie post-purchase survey answers to the order they came from?
faq_plan.a: Put the order number in the survey link, for example ?order=48213. Each answer then saves with the order it belongs to, even when the buyer opens the link on another device. From there, join each answer to that order's products and ship date, and filter the results by either one.

faq_plan.q: Should post purchase surveys differ for first-time and repeat buyers?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask first-time buyers how they found the store, since that answer only matters once. Ask repeat buyers what brings them back or what they would like you to stock next, and skip the source question. Tag each response with the buyer's order count so the dashboard can split the two groups.

faq_plan.q: Can a post-purchase survey be just one question?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A single question with fixed options works much like poll questions: quick to answer and easy to count. Pick the one whose answer changes a decision, such as where the buyer heard of the store, and add Other with a short text box for answers you did not list.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is question lists, how-tos and store apps; page gives a 7-step how-to ('01 Pick the decision each question feeds' to '07 Publish and read the first week'), four worked examples (order source, delivery check, fit, reorder timing) and FAQ items on question count, examples, timing and tying answers to orders.

specificity.evidence: Store vocabulary throughout: 'order confirmation page', 'carrier marks a Pantrywell box delivered', 'Talus hiking pant', '?order=48213', 'ship date'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Wickfern Candle Co. asks first-time buyers...', 'When the carrier marks a Pantrywell box delivered...', 'Describe the store, the product, and the decision...'.

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; QC Q2 flags only (feature_5 34 words, tab_content_4 33, FAQ 5 36). Hyphenation inconsistency logged as a note.

voice.evidence: Plain, specific, unglamorous detail: 'a broken jar or a short shipment', 'Order 48213, delivered today'. Two forced anchors logged as notes.
